questions.question: A horse rider covers half the distance with $5m{s}^{- 1}$ speed. The remaining part of the distance was travelled with speed $10m{s}^{- 1}$ for half the time and with speed $15m{s}^{- 1}$ for other half of the time. The mean speed of the rider averaged over the whole time of motion is $\dfrac{x}{7}m{s}^{- 1}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution:
Let total distance travelled by horse rider be $2x$.

Now, the time taken to cover first half distance is ${t}_{AB} = \dfrac{x}{5}$

Second half distance $x$ between $BC$ is covered in two parts, $x = {d}_{1} + {d}_{2}$

here ${d}_{1}$ is the distance travelled with $10m{s}^{- 1}$ and ${d}_{2}$ is the distance travelled with $15m{s}^{- 1}$ in equal time intervals $\dfrac{t}{2}$ each.

Then, ${d}_{1} = \dfrac{10t}{2}, {d}_{2} = \dfrac{15t}{2}$

Second half distance $x = \dfrac{t}{2} ( 10 + 15 ) = \dfrac{25t}{2}$

Now, the mean speed of rider is $v = \dfrac{2x}{\dfrac{x}{5} + \dfrac{2x}{25}} = \dfrac{2 \times 25}{5 + 2} = \dfrac{50}{7}m{s}^{- 1}$

Thus, the value of $x = 50$.

$⇒ \dfrac{dv}{dt} = - 2\alpha{v}^{3}\left[\text{as}v = \dfrac{dx}{dt}\right] ⇒ a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = - 2\alpha{v}^{3}$

questions.question:
A particle starts moving from time $t=0$ and its coordinate is given as $x(t)=4 t^{3}-3 t$
A. The particle returns to its original position (origin) 0.866 units later
B. The particle is 1 unit away from origin at its turning point
C. Acceleration of the particle is non-negative
D. The particle is 0.5 units away from origin at its turning point
E. Particle never turns back as acceleration is non-negative
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Given $x(t) = 4t^3 - 3t$, we find $v(t) = 12t^2 - 3$ and $a(t) = 24t$.
Statement A: Setting $x(t) = 0$ gives $4t^3 - 3t = 0 \Rightarrow t(4t^2-3) = 0$, so $t = 0$ or $t = \sqrt{3/4} = 0.866$. The particle returns to origin at $t = 0.866$ units. TRUE.
Statement B: Turning points occur at $v(t) = 0 \Rightarrow 12t^2 - 3 = 0 \Rightarrow t = \pm 0.5$. At $t = 0.5$: $x = 4(0.125) - 1.5 = -1$; distance = 1 unit. At $t = -0.5$: $x = 1$; distance = 1 unit. TRUE.
Statement C: For $t \geq 0$ (particle starts at $t=0$), $a(t) = 24t \geq 0$. TRUE.
Statement D: At turning points, distance is 1 unit, not 0.5. FALSE.
Statement E: False because acceleration is non-negative only for $t \geq 0$, and particle does turn back at $t = 0.5$. FALSE.
Correct statements: A, B, C Only.

Given,
Initially both car is at rest, so ${u}_{1} = {u}_{2} = 0$
Acceleration of car $A \text{ and } B$ is ${a}_{1} \text{ and } {a}_{2}$

Let us assume,
Time of reach to destination of car $A$ is, ${t}_{1} = {t}_{0}$
Time of reach to destination of car $B$ is, ${t}_{2} = {t}_{0} + t$

Using second equation of motion, we have
${u}_{1}t + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{1}{t}_{1}^{2} = {u}_{2}t + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{2}{t2}^{2}$
$⇒ 0 \times t + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{1}{t}_{0}^{2} = 0 \times t + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{2}\left({t}_{0} + t\right)2$
$⇒ \sqrt{\dfrac{a1}{a2}}{t}_{0} = {t}_{0} + t$

Equation (1) implies that

$0 = \left(\dfrac{2u}{3}\right)2 + 2\left(- a\right)\left(x\right) . . . \left(3\right)$

Hence, $D = 32$.

$117 = \dfrac{9a_2}{2} \Rightarrow a_2 = 26$ m/s$^2$

$v_2 = u_2 + a_2 t = 12 + 26 \times 10 = 272$ m/s

$p_2 = m_2 v_2 = 2.5 \times 272 = 680$ kg m/s

Ratio of their momenta:
$\dfrac{p_1}{p_2} = \dfrac{765}{680} = \dfrac{9}{8}$

During the first $2\text{ s}$ of free fall, the paratrooper starts from rest ($u = 0$).
Velocity after $2\text{ s}$ is $v_1 = u + gt = 0 + 10 \times 2 = 20\text{ m/s}$.
Distance covered during free fall is $h_1 = \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 2^2 = 20\text{ m}$.
After opening the parachute, the paratrooper decelerates at $a = -3\text{ m/s}^2$.
At a height of $10\text{ m}$ from the ground, the final velocity is $v_2 = 5\text{ m/s}$.

$5^2 = 20^2 + 2(-3)h_2$
$25 = 400 - 6h_2$
$6h_2 = 375$

The total height of the airplane is the sum of the free fall distance, the deceleration distance, and the remaining height from the ground.
$H = h_1 + h_2 + 10 = 20 + 62.5 + 10 = 92.5\text{ m}$.

questions.question: A ball is thrown up vertically with a certain velocity so that, it reaches a maximum height $h$. Find the ratio of the times in which it is at height $\dfrac{h}{3}$ while going up and coming down respectively.
questions.solution:
The maximum height of a projectile thrown vertically upward is given by, $h = \dfrac{u2}{2g}$.

$⇒ u = \sqrt{2gh}$

Using equation of motion with constant acceleration,

$s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}a{t}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{h}{3} = \sqrt{2gh}t - \dfrac{1}{2}g{t}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{g{t}^{2}}{2} - \sqrt{2ght} + \dfrac{h}{3} = 0$

Solving the above quadratic equation we will get the times ${t}_{1}$ and ${t}_{2}$. $⇒ \dfrac{t2}{t1} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2gh} + \sqrt{2gh - 4 \times \dfrac{g}{2} \times \dfrac{h}{3}}}{\sqrt{2gh} - \sqrt{2gh - 4 \times \dfrac{g}{2} \times \dfrac{h}{3}}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2gh} + \sqrt{\dfrac{4gh}{3}}}{\sqrt{2gh} - \sqrt{\dfrac{4gh}{3}}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}$

Thus, the ratio $\dfrac{t1}{t2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}}$

questions.question: A body starts falling freely from height $H$ hits an inclined plane in its path at height $h$. As a result of this perfectly elastic impact, the direction of the velocity of the body becomes horizontal. The value of $\dfrac{H}{h}$ for which the body will take the maximum time to reach the ground is _____.
questions.solution:
Total time of flight $= T$ can be written as, 

$T = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}} + \sqrt{\dfrac{2\left(H - h\right)}{g}}$

For maximum time $= \dfrac{dT}{dh} = 0$

$⇒ \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{g}}\left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{h}} - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{H - h}}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \sqrt{H - h} = \sqrt{h}$

$⇒ h = \dfrac{H}{2} ⇒ \dfrac{H}{h} = 2$

questions.solution:
Time for first drop to fall 5 m:
$5 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times t^2$ gives $t = 1$ s.
Since the first drop strikes when the sixth begins, there are 5 intervals: each interval $T = \frac{1}{5} = 0.2$ s.
When drop 1 hits the ground (at $t = 1$ s), drop 4 has been falling for $t_4 = 1 - 3 \times 0.2 = 0.4$ s.
Distance fallen by drop 4: $s_4 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times (0.4)^2 = 0.8$ m.
Height of drop 4 above ground: $5 - 0.8 = 4.2$ m.

questions.question: A gas balloon is going up with a constant velocity of $10$ m/s. When this balloon reached a height of $75$ m, a stone is dropped from it and balloon keeps moving up with the same velocity. The height of the balloon when the stone hits the ground is ________ m. (Take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
When the stone is dropped, it acquires the initial velocity of the balloon. Taking the upward direction as positive, the initial velocity of the stone is $u = 10$ m/s.

The displacement of the stone when it hits the ground is $S = -75$ m, and its acceleration is $a = -g = -10$ m/s$^2$.

Using the equation of motion $S = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^2$:

$-75 = 10t - \dfrac{1}{2}(10)t^2$

$-75 = 10t - 5t^2$

$5t^2 - 10t - 75 = 0$

$t^2 - 2t - 15 = 0$

$(t - 5)(t + 3) = 0$

Since time cannot be negative, $t = 5$ s.

During this time, the balloon continues to move upwards with a constant velocity of $10$ m/s. The distance travelled by the balloon in $5$ s is:

$d = v \times t = 10 \times 5 = 50$ m

The total height of the balloon when the stone hits the ground is:

$H = 75 + 50 = 125$ m

Answer: $125$

If train $A$ take $35s$ less time than train $B$ to cross the tunnel then, length $L$ of tunnel is:

(Given $L = 60l$)
questions.solution:
The time taken for $A$

$\Delta{t}_{A} = \dfrac{l + L}{VA}$

The time taken for $B$

$\Delta{t}_{B} = \dfrac{4l + L}{VB}$

It is given that $B$ takes more time than $A$. So,

$⇒ \dfrac{4l + L}{20} - \dfrac{l + L}{30} = 35$

$⇒ \dfrac{64l}{20} - \dfrac{61l}{30} = 35$

$⇒ l = \dfrac{35 \times 600}{700} = 30m$

Therefore,

$L = 1800m$.

questions.question: Two cars $A$ and $B$ are moving in the same direction along a straight line with speeds $100$ km/h and $80$ km/h, respectively such that car $A$ is moving ahead of car $B$. A person in car $B$ throws a stone with a speed $v$ so that it hits the car $A$ with a speed of $5$ m/s. The value of $v$ is ______ km/h.
questions.solution:
Velocity of car A, $v_A = 100$ km/h

Velocity of car B, $v_B = 80$ km/h

Velocity of the stone relative to car B is $v$. The velocity of the stone relative to the ground is $v_S = v_B + v = 80 + v$.

The velocity of the stone relative to car A is $v_{S/A} = v_S - v_A = (80 + v) - 100 = v - 20$.

The stone hits car A with a relative speed of $5$ m/s. Converting this speed to km/h:

$v_{S/A} = 5 \times \dfrac{18}{5} = 18$ km/h

Equating the relative speeds:

$v - 20 = 18 \Rightarrow v = 38$ km/h

Answer: $38$

questions.q: A river of width 200 m is flowing from west to east with a speed of $18 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$. A boat, moving with speed of $36 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ in still water, is made to travel one-round trip (bank to bank of the river). Minimum time taken by the boat for this journey and also the displacement along the river bank are $\_\_\_\_$ and $\_\_\_\_$ respectively.
questions.question: A river of width 200 m is flowing from west to east with a speed of $18 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$. A boat, moving with speed of $36 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ in still water, is made to travel one-round trip (bank to bank of the river). Minimum time taken by the boat for this journey and also the displacement along the river bank are $\_\_\_\_$ and $\_\_\_\_$ respectively.
questions.solution:
Width of the river $d = 200$ m.
Speed of river $v_r = 18$ km/h $= 18 \times \frac{5}{18} = 5$ m/s.
Speed of boat in still water $v_b = 36$ km/h $= 36 \times \frac{5}{18} = 10$ m/s.
For minimum time to cross the river, the boat must head perpendicular to the river flow (at $90^\circ$ to the bank).
Time taken to cross once $t = \frac{d}{v_b} = \frac{200}{10} = 20$ s.
For a round trip (bank to bank and back), the total minimum time is $T = 2t = 2 \times 20 = 40$ s.
During the first crossing, the drift (displacement along the bank) is $x_1 = v_r \times t = 5 \times 20 = 100$ m.
During the return trip, to minimize time, the boat again heads perpendicular to the flow relative to the water. The river continues to flow in the same direction, so the drift is again in the same direction as the first trip.
Return drift $x_2 = v_r \times t = 5 \times 20 = 100$ m.
Total displacement along the river bank $= x_1 + x_2 = 100 + 100 = 200$ m.
Thus, minimum time is $40$ s and displacement is $200$ m.

questions.question: Two identical bodies, projected with the same speed at two different angles cover the same horizontal range $R$. If the time of flight of these bodies are $5$ s and $10$ s, respectively, then the value of $R$ is ________ m. (Take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
For two projectiles to have the same horizontal range $R$ with the same initial speed $u$, their angles of projection must be complementary, i.e., $\theta$ and $90^\circ - \theta$.

The times of flight for these two angles are given by:
$t_1 = \dfrac{2u \sin \theta}{g}$
$t_2 = \dfrac{2u \cos \theta}{g}$

Multiplying $t_1$ and $t_2$, we get:
$t_1 t_2 = \left(\dfrac{2u \sin \theta}{g}\right) \left(\dfrac{2u \cos \theta}{g}\right) = \dfrac{2}{g} \left(\dfrac{u^2 (2 \sin \theta \cos \theta)}{g}\right)$

Since the horizontal range is $R = \dfrac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{g}$, we can write:
$t_1 t_2 = \dfrac{2R}{g}$

Given $t_1 = 5$ s, $t_2 = 10$ s, and $g = 10$ m/s$^2$, substituting these values:
$5 \times 10 = \dfrac{2R}{10}$

$50 = \dfrac{2R}{10}$

$2R = 500 \Rightarrow R = 250$ m

Answer: $250$
